spans.s: bāra (EI 13), Telugu; the distance between the ends of out-stretched arms.
bārāḍ, derived from Sanskrit varāṭa or varāṭaka, ‘a cowrie-shell (used as money)’ (JNSI, Vol. XVI, p. 18). Cf. varāṭikā.
barāḍ , modified form of varāṭaka (q. v.).
baraṭa (CII 4), a plant grown for fencing.
Barkandāz, Persian; same as Pāik (q. v.).
bartanā (IE 3-5), Rājasthānī; a blunt stick for writing on a wooden slate; same as barthā.
bārah-gānī , 1(1/2) aṭha-gānīs; billon coin equal to 12 copper jitals and to (1/4) of the silver ṭaṅka
